title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: A CONCESSION IS TWO MOVES, NOT ONE CLAUSE. Grant the point flat, then turn: C'est vrai que c'est cher, mais … / Tu as raison, en revanche … Everyday French never buries the concession in a subordinate clause, so the shape of an argument here is a sequence of short statements rather than one long sentence.

ENGLISH CONCEDES WITH although AND FRENCH DOES NOT. The learner reaches for bien que, which is real French, takes a mood this ladder has not opened, and is almost never spoken. Naming it and refusing it is worth more than teaching it: say the concession flat and turn after the comma.

THE TURN WORDS SPLIT BY REGISTER, AND THE SPLIT IS THE CONTENT. par contre is what is said, en revanche what is written. pourtant and cependant carry a real and yet. quand même goes at the END of its clause and means all the same. All four join the same two facts; picking the wrong one is a mistake of clothing.

on the other hand IS NOT de l'autre côté. French has only the PAIR — d'un côté … de l'autre — and it must open with d'un côté for the second half to mean anything. de l'autre côté exists and means on the other side, of a street or a river, which is a place and not an argument.

actually IS en fait, NEVER actuellement. actuellement means currently, so Actuellement je ne suis pas d'accord says I am not agreeing at the moment — a different claim and a softer one. This is the flattest false friend in the course, and it costs a whole sentence when it goes wrong.

il vaut mieux AND il faudrait TAKE A BARE INFINITIVE AND NAME NOBODY. Il vaut mieux partir plus tôt, il faudrait attendre demain — no de, no subject, no finger pointed. That impersonal frame is what makes advice persuasive here rather than bossy, and it is the cheapest thing in the module.

EVERY CLAUSE IN THIS MODULE STAYS INDICATIVE AND EVERY NEGATIVE KEEPS ITS ne. Je ne suis pas d'accord. No turn word — mais, pourtant, en revanche, par contre, cependant — moves the mood of the verb behind it, and none of them is a reason to drop a ne that L1-M3 put there.

sentences.display: C'est vrai que le train est cher, mais il est plus rapide
sentences.cue: It's true the train is expensive, but it's faster
sentences.literal: It-is true that the train is expensive, but it is more fast

words.note: The flat grant. It concedes the other side's fact whole, and the que is not optional — English drops that, French keeps que.
One form for both genders, like tranquille. Comparatives are L2-M9's plus: plus rapide, moins rapide, nothing new to build.

sentences.trap: The concession is a complete sentence before the comma. Nothing about c'est vrai que weakens it — you are agreeing, and the mais is what buys it back.
sentences.sound: seh VREH kuh luh TRAN eh SHEHR, meh eel eh plew ra-PEED. plus keeps its s before a vowel here, so plus rapide is plew-ra-PEED with no z.

variations.display: C'est vrai que c'est cher, mais c'est plus rapide
variations.cue: It's true it's expensive, but it's faster
variations.changed: the subject drops to c'est on both sides, which is how it is usually said

variations.display: C'est vrai que le train est cher, mais il est plus tranquille
variations.cue: It's true the train is expensive, but it's quieter
variations.changed: a different virtue bought back, on the same two-move frame

mistake.display: Bien que le train soit cher, il est plus rapide
mistake.why: bien que is real French, takes a mood this ladder has not opened, and almost nobody says it out loud. Grant the point flat, then turn.

sentences.usage: The opening move of any argument you expect to win: the other side hears their own point back before they hear yours.

sentences.display: Tu as raison, en revanche c'est trop cher
sentences.cue: You're right, on the other hand it's too expensive
sentences.literal: You have reason, in revenge it-is too expensive

words.note: raison is a noun, so French HAS reason rather than being right. Indexed whole here; raison itself is already L3-M3's row, from ait raison.
The written turn. Same job as par contre and one register up, so it belongs in an email and sounds careful out loud.

sentences.trap: Conceding first costs you nothing and buys the turn. en revanche needs something granted in front of it, or there is nothing for it to turn away from.
sentences.sound: tew a reh-ZON, on ruh-VONSH seh troh SHEHR. revanche ends in the soft sh of chose, and the en in front is nasal.

variations.display: Tu as raison, en revanche c'est très loin
variations.cue: You're right, on the other hand it's very far
variations.changed: a different objection hung on the same turn

variations.display: Tu as raison, en revanche je préfère le train
variations.cue: You're right, on the other hand I prefer the train
variations.changed: the turn carries a preference instead of a fact

mistake.display: Tu es raison, en revanche c'est trop cher
mistake.why: raison is a noun and goes with avoir. Tu es raison says you ARE a reason; it is tu as raison, always.

sentences.usage: The safest disagreement in the language — it is heard as fair rather than as opposition.

sentences.display: Certes, c'est plus cher, pourtant je préfère le train
sentences.cue: Granted, it's more expensive, and yet I prefer the train
sentences.literal: Certainly, it-is more expensive, however I prefer the train

words.note: A one-word concession that opens the sentence. It is a shade formal and it always promises a turn — nobody says certes and then stops.
The real and yet: it marks the turn as surprising, not merely opposite. It joins two full clauses on its own and never takes que.

sentences.trap: certes and pourtant are a matched pair. Opening with certes and turning with mais is not wrong, but it wastes the promise certes made.
sentences.sound: SEHRT, seh plew SHEHR, poor-TON zhuh pray-FEHR luh TRAN. certes keeps its final t, which is unusual and worth remembering.

variations.display: Certes, c'est plus cher, pourtant c'est plus rapide
variations.cue: Granted, it's more expensive, and yet it's faster
variations.changed: the turn carries a second comparison rather than a preference

variations.display: Certes, c'est loin, pourtant c'est tranquille
variations.cue: Granted, it's far, and yet it's quiet
variations.changed: both halves shorten to c'est, which is the spoken shape

mistake.display: Certes, c'est plus cher, pourtant que je préfère le train
mistake.why: pourtant joins two clauses by itself. Adding que turns it into a subordinator it has never been.

sentences.usage: Written French, and spoken French when somebody is being deliberately reasonable. It signals that the argument is not over.

sentences.display: D'un côté c'est pratique, de l'autre c'est très cher
sentences.cue: On one hand it's practical, on the other it's very expensive
sentences.literal: Of one side it-is practical, of the other it-is very expensive

words.note: The opener of a pair. It commits you to a second half — start with it and the listener is already waiting for de l'autre.
The closer, and it stops there: de l'autre côté means on the other SIDE, of a street or a river, and is not this phrase.
One form for both genders. Said of a thing that saves you trouble, far more often than English says practical.

sentences.trap: The two halves are one structure, not two sentences that happen to be near each other. Drop d'un côté and de l'autre has nothing to answer.
sentences.sound: dun koh-TAY seh pra-TEEK, duh LOH-truh seh treh SHEHR. côté ends in a clean ay; the circumflex is history, not sound.

variations.display: D'un côté c'est rapide, de l'autre c'est cher
variations.cue: On one hand it's fast, on the other it's expensive
variations.changed: the two sides swap in a different pair of facts

variations.display: D'un côté c'est pratique, de l'autre c'est trop loin
variations.cue: On one hand it's handy, on the other it's too far
variations.changed: the objection becomes distance rather than price

mistake.display: D'un côté c'est pratique, de l'autre côté c'est très cher
mistake.why: The pair is d'un côté … de l'autre. Putting côté back in makes it a place — on the other side of the street — which is not what you meant.

sentences.usage: How a French speaker shows they have weighed something. It reads as fair-minded even when the second half is the one you believe.
sentences.mnemonic: The second side loses its côté.

sentences.display: Il vaut mieux partir plus tôt
sentences.literal: It is-worth better to-leave more early

words.note: Impersonal advice that names nobody: the il is empty. It takes a bare infinitive with no de, and mieux is already L2-M9's word.

sentences.trap: No de between the frame and the verb. il vaut mieux partir, never il vaut mieux de partir — the infinitive attaches straight on.
sentences.sound: eel voh myuh par-TEER plew TOH. vaut is one syllable, voh, with no t heard at all.

variations.display: Il vaut mieux attendre demain
variations.cue: It's better to wait until tomorrow
variations.changed: the advice becomes patience, on the same empty il

variations.display: Il vaut mieux prendre le train
variations.cue: It's better to take the train
variations.changed: the infinitive takes an object and the frame does not move

mistake.display: Il vaut mieux de partir plus tôt
mistake.why: il vaut mieux takes the infinitive bare. The de is English's to leaking in through it is better TO leave.

sentences.usage: The persuasive move that avoids an argument: advice with no subject is hard to take personally.

sentences.display: Je suis d'accord, par contre je préfère le vélo
sentences.cue: I agree, that said I prefer the bike
sentences.literal: I am of-agreement, by against I prefer the bike

words.cue: that said, on the other hand
words.note: The spoken turn, and the one you will actually hear. Same job as en revanche one register down; in writing, prefer en revanche.

sentences.trap: par contre turns after you have granted something. au contraire contradicts what was just said, so the two are not swappable even though English blurs them.
sentences.sound: zhuh swee da-KOR, par KON-truh zhuh pray-FEHR luh vay-LOH. contre ends in a swallowed ruh, barely a syllable.

variations.display: Je suis d'accord, par contre je préfère le train
variations.cue: I agree, that said I prefer the train
variations.changed: the preference changes and the concession holds

variations.display: Je suis d'accord, par contre c'est trop cher
variations.cue: I agree, that said it's too expensive
variations.changed: the turn carries an objection instead of a preference

mistake.display: Je suis d'accord, au contraire je préfère le vélo
mistake.why: au contraire denies what was just said, and you have just agreed with it. The word that turns after a concession is par contre.

sentences.usage: Ordinary spoken French, and a shade too casual for a report — the same sentence written takes en revanche.
sentences.mnemonic: par contre turns; au contraire denies.

sentences.display: C'est cher, cependant c'est le meilleur restaurant de la ville
sentences.cue: It's expensive, however it's the best restaurant in town
sentences.literal: It-is expensive, however it-is the best restaurant of the city

words.note: pourtant's written twin, and the most neutral of the turns. It carries the same and yet, with none of par contre's spoken feel.

sentences.trap: cependant already contains the mais. Writing mais cependant is not emphasis; it is the same word twice.
sentences.sound: seh SHEHR, suh-pon-DON seh luh meh-YUR res-toh-RON duh la VEEL. cependant is three flat syllables with the stress only on the last.

variations.display: C'est cher, cependant c'est le meilleur
variations.cue: It's expensive, however it's the best
variations.changed: the noun drops and le meilleur stands alone

variations.display: C'est loin, cependant c'est le meilleur restaurant de la ville
variations.cue: It's far, however it's the best restaurant in town
variations.changed: the concession changes and the turn does not

mistake.display: C'est cher, mais cependant c'est le meilleur restaurant de la ville
mistake.why: cependant is already the turn. Stacking mais in front of it doubles the word rather than strengthening it.

sentences.usage: The written register. In speech the same sentence takes mais, and nobody would notice the difference.

sentences.display: C'est plus cher, mais je préfère le train quand même
sentences.cue: It's more expensive, but I prefer the train all the same
sentences.literal: It-is more expensive, but I prefer the train when same

words.note: It closes the clause it softens rather than opening it. Two words, and neither one carries its ordinary meaning inside the pair.

sentences.trap: quand même lands at the END. Every other turn word in this module opens its clause, and this is the one that does not.
sentences.sound: seh plew SHEHR, meh zhuh pray-FEHR luh tran kon-MEM. quand même runs together as kon-MEM, with the d never heard.

variations.display: C'est plus cher, mais je préfère le vélo quand même
variations.cue: It's more expensive, but I prefer the bike all the same
variations.changed: the choice changes and the closing position does not

variations.display: C'est loin, mais je préfère ce restaurant quand même
variations.cue: It's far, but I prefer this restaurant all the same
variations.changed: the concession becomes distance and quand même still closes

mistake.display: C'est plus cher, mais quand même je préfère le train
mistake.why: Fronted, quand même reads as an exclamation of protest rather than a softener. The all the same sense is the one that closes the sentence.

sentences.usage: How a French speaker holds their ground without escalating: it grants the objection and keeps the decision.

sentences.display: Tu as raison, mais en fait je ne suis pas d'accord
sentences.cue: You're right, but actually I don't agree
sentences.literal: You have reason, but in fact I not am not of-agreement

words.note: The word English means by actually. actuellement means currently and is a different claim — this is the course's flattest false friend.

sentences.trap: en fait corrects; actuellement dates. Swap them and I don't agree becomes I am not agreeing at the moment, which concedes far more than you meant.
sentences.sound: tew a reh-ZON, meh on FEHT zhuh nuh swee pah da-KOR. en fait keeps its t, unlike most French words ending that way.

variations.display: Tu as raison, mais en fait je préfère attendre
variations.cue: You're right, but actually I'd rather wait
variations.changed: the correction becomes a preference rather than a refusal

variations.display: Certes, mais en fait je ne suis pas d'accord
variations.cue: Granted, but actually I don't agree
variations.changed: the concession moves up a register and the rest holds

mistake.display: Tu as raison, mais actuellement je ne suis pas d'accord
mistake.why: actuellement is currently. That sentence says you are not agreeing for now, which is a concession you did not intend to make.

sentences.usage: The softest way to refuse outright: the concession is real, and en fait marks the refusal as a correction rather than a fight.

sentences.display: De toute façon, il faudrait attendre demain
sentences.cue: In any case, we'd have to wait until tomorrow
sentences.literal: Of all fashion, it would-be-necessary to-wait tomorrow

words.note: It closes an argument by making the branches irrelevant. façon is a way of doing something; the phrase is fixed and never takes a plural.

words.cue: we'd have to, it would take
words.note: The conditional of falloir, with an empty il. Like il vaut mieux it takes a bare infinitive and names nobody, which is what softens it.

sentences.trap: il faudrait has no subject to argue with. English has to name somebody — we would have to — and French does not, which is exactly why it lands gently.
sentences.sound: duh toot fa-ZON, eel foh-DREH a-TON-druh duh-MAN. façon has the soft c of the cedilla, so it is fa-ZON and never fa-KON.

variations.display: De toute façon, il faudrait partir plus tôt
variations.cue: In any case, we'd have to leave earlier
variations.changed: the necessary action changes and the frame does not

variations.display: De toute façon, il vaut mieux attendre
variations.cue: In any case, it's better to wait
variations.changed: necessity softens into advice, on the same empty il

mistake.display: De toute façon, il faudrait d'attendre demain
mistake.why: il faudrait takes the infinitive bare, exactly like il vaut mieux. There is no de between the frame and the verb.

sentences.usage: The move that ends a discussion without winning it — it says the disagreement no longer decides anything.
